headline: High-risk filesystem and MCP overlap: Gemini CLI can write/egress while the paired profile is unverified and non-runnable, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is non-runnable and has no shared channel documented, but Agent B can read/write the filesystem and use MCP, so a shared workspace or MCP bridge could let attacker-controlled content influence B. The pathway is plausible but not proven by A’s profile alone, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Agent A’s outputs are copied into a shared file or MCP resource that Agent B reads
IF Agent B is pointed at a directory containing attacker-controlled content
mitigations: Disable shared workspace handoff between agents
Require manual review before B reads any A-generated file
Run B in a separate directory
Restrict MCP servers to trusted, read-only endpoints
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all inter-agent files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B has broad network egress and reads files in the cwd, while Agent A’s profile is sparse and non-runnable. If sensitive files are placed in a shared workspace, B can transmit them to external APIs; A does not add a second leak path, but the pair still creates a default leakage risk through B.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the directory B reads
IF B is allowed to send file contents to external model APIs
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of B’s working directory
Use a redacted copy of the workspace
Disable network egress for the session
Review B’s prompts before execution
requires-engineering: enforce per-file data-loss controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent B can write the filesystem and modify git state, and its concurrency model says shared state with other instances is via filesystem and git only. Agent A has no write surface, but if the pair is used in the same repo, B’s default write and git capabilities create direct conflict and overwrite risk; uncertainty about A’s runtime does not reduce this.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same repository or directory
IF B is run concurrently with another writer to the same git state
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git branches per agent
Require explicit commit approval
requires-engineering: add locking around shared git and filesystem writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent B can act on files and shell commands, so if it treats A-derived content as authoritative, errors can cascade into edits or commands. Agent A is only a collection profile and cannot verify anything itself, making the pair vulnerable to unverified handoff rather than direct autonomous harm.
conditions: IF B consumes A-generated text as instructions or facts
IF B is allowed to execute shell or file edits based on that text
mitigations: Require a human verification step before B acts
Mark A outputs as untrusted by default
Limit B to read-only mode for review tasks
Use structured output with explicit provenance fields
requires-engineering: add verification gates before action-taking

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for Agent A, while Agent B handles Google API keys and can send data to Google services. Because the pair lacks explicit compliance metadata, only a limited low-severity concern is supportable; the other agent is not cited for a concrete mismatch.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into B’s prompts or files
IF the deployment requires residency or retention guarantees not provided by Google APIs
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the session
Review vendor terms before use
Disable optional Google account login
Use local-only test data
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
